claims.text: Conventional pressureless sintering of single-phase ZrB2 requires temperatures above 2300 °C.
Conventionally pressureless-sintered ZrB2 has significant porosity.
Conventionally pressureless-sintered ZrB2 has suboptimal mechanical integrity.
SPS can consolidate single-phase ZrB2 at approximately 1800–2000 °C under applied pressure and an inert atmosphere.
Replacing pressureless sintering above 2300 °C with SPS will lower the required ZrB2 preparation temperature.
SPS will produce ZrB2 with higher density than conventional pressureless sintering.
SPS will produce ZrB2 with fewer residual pores and porosity defects than conventional pressureless sintering.
Rapid heating and applied pressure during SPS enhance atomic diffusion and densification at lower temperatures.
SPS suppresses excessive grain growth during consolidation of ZrB2.
SPS suppresses pore formation during consolidation of ZrB2.
The denser, less porous SPS microstructure will be more uniform and mechanically robust.
Reduced porosity and improved mechanical robustness will minimize hole formation during exposure to a corrosive liquid plating bath.
SPS-processed ZrB2 will have greater mechanical strength than conventionally pressureless-sintered ZrB2.
SPS-processed ZrB2 will better resist degradation during long-duration liquid plating bath exposure.
Existing porosity in conventionally prepared ZrB2 contributes to component failure under liquid plating bath service.
SPS pressure and heating rate may influence the final performance of the ceramic.
